the friction of a sliding contact can be identified from the instantaneous dynamic forces, which is useful to identify optimum operating conditions of a sliding contact.
the coefficient of friction of a graphite electric sliding contact can be determined by measuring the instantaneous forces, the contact temperature, and the electrical current density.

identifying the frictional forces of a graphite electric contact for different operating conditions.
the identification of the COF for the contact of a graphite electric sliding brush with a commutator under different conditions.

the coefficient of friction can be determined for different contact temperatures, electric current densities and contact pressures by the presented procedures.

the dynamic friction force of the graphite–copper brush contact is a function of the contact temperature and the electric contact current density.
